rows.statement: Across Michigan and New York counties, County Health Rankings & Roadmaps 2025 premature age-adjusted mortality (v127: deaths under age 75 per 100,000, age-adjusted; NCHS death records 2020-2022, Census Population Estimates denominators) is higher where the ACS 2018-2022 poverty rate is higher, with state intercepts; coefficient corrected for ACS sampling error in the covariate (fit_eiv; the outcome is an external direct estimate held fixed).

Conditional on the poverty rate, the share of adults 25+ with a bachelor's degree or higher, the housing cost-burden share and state, county premature age-adjusted mortality is higher where a larger share of occupied housing units has no vehicle available (fit_eiv).

Conditional on the poverty rate, the bachelor's share, the no-vehicle share and state, county premature age-adjusted mortality is higher where a larger share of households spends 30% or more of income on housing costs (fit_eiv).

Across Michigan and New York counties, premature age-adjusted mortality is higher where age-standardized disability prevalence (all ages, 2000 U.S. standard population, ACS 2018-2022) is higher, with state intercepts (fit_eiv).
